beginner.summary: For developers, analysts and IT staff who want to run large language models on their own machine and have not used Ollama before. Covers installation on Windows, macOS and Linux, pulling and running models from the library, model tags and sizes, the interactive session, storage and context length, sampling options, system prompts, first Modelfiles, the local server on port 11434, the REST API with curl, the Python and JavaScript libraries, JSON output, embeddings, Open WebUI, and a command-line assistant capstone.
prerequisites: Uses a terminal confidently: running commands, setting environment variables and reading text output
Has read basic Python or JavaScript and can run a short script
Has a laptop or workstation with at least 16 GB of RAM, 20 GB of free disk and rights to install software (a discrete GPU is helpful but not required)
outcomes: Install Ollama, pull models and run them from the command line while choosing a model size that fits the machine
Customise behaviour with sampling options, system prompts and simple Modelfiles
Call the local REST API with curl and the official Python and JavaScript libraries, including streaming, JSON output and embeddings
Build and test a small local chat tool that works without internet access after the first model download

advanced.summary: For platform, DevOps and senior application engineers who run Ollama for teams or in production. Covers Docker and Docker Compose with GPU access, Kubernetes deployment and operations, securing exposed endpoints with reverse proxies, TLS, API keys and network policy, multi-GPU scheduling, load testing, observability, troubleshooting, embedding pipelines at scale, hybrid retrieval, local agents, LangChain and LlamaIndex integration, model lifecycle and air-gapped operation, comparison with other serving stacks, regression testing, and a production runbook capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the intermediate Ollama material or runs Ollama with custom models, tools and a retrieval pipeline
Knows Docker, a reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy and basic Kubernetes objects (Deployment, Service, PersistentVolumeClaim)
Has access to a Linux host with an NVIDIA GPU and the container toolkit, or a Kubernetes cluster with GPU nodes, for the deployment exercises
outcomes: Deploy Ollama in containers and on Kubernetes with persistent models, GPU scheduling, probes and resource limits
Secure an Ollama endpoint with TLS, authentication, rate limits and network controls, and prove the controls work with tests
Operate Ollama with load tests, metrics, log analysis and a troubleshooting playbook
Integrate Ollama into LangChain and LlamaIndex applications and deliver a release process with regression gates
